text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing intermittent 503s from Datadog exporter since 06:00 UTC. A bunch of traces are getting routed to Tempo fallback which then doubles up in our downstream because of mismatched sampling flags. Any quick wins?

devin: Yikes. Where are the 503s originating — our egress or Datadog-side?

maria: Looks like Datadog returns 503 on /v1/traces when payloads > ~1.2MB. Smaller payloads succeed.

sanjay: That would explain the chunked traces failing. We batch aggressively in the collector for throughput.

alyssa: We could tune continuous batching to a lower max_batch_bytes for Datadog routes. Or add a prioritized routing policy: if Datadog rejects, pause sends and route to Tempo but mark as "fallback" so downstream dedupe works.

maria: Marking fallback sounds good but we also need to avoid double-counting when both accept — currently both exporters may accept same span id.

devin: What about request-level id + header when sending to exporters? Add header X-Redwood-Exported-By: datadog|tempo and downstream can drop duplicates based on (trace_id, exporter). But that needs vendor support.

alyssa: Tempo/Jaeger don't preserve custom headers in traces. Datadog accepts attributes though — we can attach an attribute like "rw_exporter" to spans. That way downstream analysis can filter.

jordan: Adding an attribute is fine. But we still need a graceful backoff so we don't flood Tempo for brief datadog blips. Suggest exponential backoff per-route with circuit-breaker state exposed in Console.

maria: Agreed. UX ask: surface exporter circuit-breaker state & recent 5xx rate on the per-route dashboard. Ops wants to know when routing is degrading.

infra-bot: deploy: exporter-router v2 pushed to staging at 2026-03-18T06:12:02Z 

devin: Nice. Does v2 include per-route retry/backoff?

infra-bot: changelog: exporter-router v2: per-route backoff, fallback tagging, metrics export for "exporter_health" series

alyssa: For rollout, can we A/B the routing policy? e.g., 10% of customers hit new circuit breaker behavior first.

sanjay: We need to be careful with tenant isolation — some customers have different sampling configs. A/B should be per-tenant, not per-request.

maria: Also retention side-effect: Tempo fallback writes traces that we keep for 90d, while Datadog TTL is 30d. That inflates storage and confuses billing. We should add TTL override for fallback traces or tag them so retention jobs apply different TTL.

devin: Two implementation pieces: 1) exporter-router policy (json) 2) collector sets attribute and TTL routing key. Drafting quick policy snip: 

```
{
  "routes": [
    {
      "name": "datadog-primary",
      "priority": 100,
      "exporter": "datadog",
      "max_batch_bytes": 1048576,
      "circuit_breaker": {
        "failure_threshold": 0.05,
        "window_secs": 60,
        "backoff_base_ms": 1000
      },
      "fallback": "tempo-secondary",
      "fallback_tag": "rw_fallback"
    }
  ]
}
```

alyssa: That looks reasonable. Small nit: set max_batch_bytes slightly below Datadog limit to avoid 503 boundaries, like 1MB (1048576 is 1MB, ok). Also include a retry_count=0 on failure to avoid duplicate attempts.

jordan: On Console: add an "exporter health" row in route detail, graph 5xx rate, avg latency, circuit-breaker state (closed/open), and a sample trace peek showing exporter tags.

maria: Can the Console also expose a "force-fallback" toggle per-route for on-call to flip in emergencies? With audit log + TTL guard.

alyssa: We can add emergency override but it must be gated by perms. Also add a rollback button that replays to previous routing policy.

devin: One potential hazard: if fallback writes have different sampling heuristics, product analytics relying on trace counts could be skewed. Recommend we increment a counter metric "traces_routed_fallback_total" and surface it in billing dashboards.

sanjay: I'll prototype attribute injection + TTL tag in the collector today. If infra-bot can roll router v2 to canary per-tenant, we can observe behavior.

infra-bot: canary-deploy: exporter-router v2 -> 10% tenants scheduled at 2026-03-18T06:20:11Z

maria: Thanks. Please post logs if we see any repeated 413/503 patterns after canary. :eyes:

alyssa: Follow-up tasks: 1) Sanjay: collector attribute + TTL tag (PR) 2) Devin: routing policy changes + console indicators 3) Jordan: Console UI mock for emergency toggle + graphs 4) Maria: coordinate on-call runbook update.

maria: I'll update the incident runbook and add a play for "exporter primary degraded -> enable fallback -> set TTL tag -> monitor billing metric"

devin: TG, adding the policy PR link when ready.

sanjay: PR: https://git.redwood.internal/collector/+/rtr-attribute-ttl (draft)

maria: Great. Closing loop when canary metrics are in. Thanks all.
